Do not attempt detector calibration, X-ray tube adjustment, or internal component repair outside approved service procedures. Expected outcome: Unverified image-quality performance is not used for patient diagnosis.

CCR.Complaint: CT staff reported streak artifacts appearing on head studies.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a removable positioning accessory containing a dense external object in the scan field.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the interfering object, inspected the accessory, completed approved image-quality verification, and confirmed the artifact was no longer present.

title: Canon Aquilion ONE / PRISM Edition CT Scanner - Study Will Not Save, Reconstruct, or Export
description: Addresses failed study saving, reconstruction, or export caused by workstation state, storage, workflow, network communication, or software-related conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Data and Avoid Unnecessary Repeat Scans
steps.instructions: Do not repeat a patient scan solely because images are not immediately saving, reconstructing, or exporting. Preserve any available raw data, images, and study identifiers while troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Existing diagnostic data is protected and unnecessary repeat radiation is avoided.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Function Is Failing
steps.instructions: Determine whether the study fails to save locally, reconstruct, display, export to PACS, or complete more than one of these steps. Record any displayed message exactly. Expected outcome: The failed portion of the imaging workflow is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Confirm Workstation Responsiveness
steps.instructions: Verify that the operator workstation is responsive and that the CT application is not frozen or partially unresponsive. Expected outcome: A general workstation problem is identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 4. Verify Study and Patient Selection
steps.instructions: Confirm that the expected patient and study are open and that staff are attempting to save or export the intended examination. Avoid deleting, merging, or modifying patient records during troubleshooting unless required by approved policy. Expected outcome: The problem is not caused by selecting the wrong study or incomplete workflow.

steps.title: 5. Check Local System Status and Storage Indications
steps.instructions: Review normal user-accessible indicators for warnings related to storage, study processing, reconstruction queues, or unavailable resources. Do not manually delete system files or alter storage partitions. Expected outcome: Any visible storage or processing condition is identified without modifying protected system data.

steps.title: 6. Check Network Connectivity for Export Problems
steps.instructions: If local saving and reconstruction work but export fails, inspect accessible network connections and verify whether PACS or other destinations are available. Expected outcome: Local processing and network-transfer problems are separated.

steps.title: 7. Determine Whether the Problem Is Study-Specific
steps.instructions: Check whether another approved test or previously completed study can be accessed or exported without altering patient data. Do not use unrelated patient records unnecessarily. Expected outcome: The issue is narrowed to one study or confirmed to affect general system processing.

steps.title: 8. Perform an Approved Controlled Restart if Appropriate
steps.instructions: If no active reconstruction or data-preservation concern prevents it, and approved procedures allow, perform a controlled workstation or system restart. Do not restart if doing so could jeopardize unsaved or unrecoverable patient data without first escalating. Expected outcome: Processing resumes without data loss and the affected functions return.

steps.title: 9. Verify Complete Study Workflow
steps.instructions: Using an appropriate approved test case, confirm that images can be acquired or accessed, reconstructed, saved, and exported to the intended destination. Confirm receipt at the destination when export is part of the complaint. Expected outcome: The complete study workflow operates normally. If achieved, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Save, Reconstruction, or Export Failure
steps.instructions: If data remains inaccessible, processing repeatedly fails, or study integrity is uncertain, remove the system from clinical use as appropriate and escalate to qualified Canon service and imaging informatics personnel. Do not manipulate databases, reconstruction software, storage arrays, or operating-system files without authorization. Expected outcome: Patient data is preserved and higher-level troubleshooting proceeds without creating additional data risk.

CCR.Complaint: CT staff reported completed studies would reconstruct normally but could not be exported to PACS.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found local image processing was normal but the approved network connection to the workstation was disconnected.
CCR.Resolution: Restored the network connection, exported an approved test study, confirmed receipt in PACS, and verified the normal study workflow.

helpfulDetails: Exact save, reconstruction, or export message.

title: Canon Aquilion ONE / PRISM Edition CT Scanner - System Will Not Power On or Complete Startup
description: Addresses no-power, incomplete startup, or failed initialization caused by power, emergency-stop, workstation, connection, or facility-related conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Preserve Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot the CT system while a patient depends on it for an active or time-critical examination. Remove the patient from the scanner area when necessary and move urgent imaging to another verified system. Confirm whether the reported problem affects the entire CT system, only the operator workstation, or one subsystem. Expected outcome: The patient is safe, an alternate imaging pathway is available, and the exact affected portion of the system is identified. If the system starts normally and remains stable after confirming the reported condition, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Startup Failure
steps.instructions: Ask clinical staff what occurred immediately before the problem. Determine whether the system is completely unresponsive, partially powered, stuck during initialization, repeatedly restarting, or displaying a specific message. Record any displayed message exactly rather than interpreting it. Expected outcome: The startup failure is reproducible or clearly characterized. If the system now completes startup normally and no abnormal condition remains, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 3. Check Facility and System Power
steps.instructions: Verify that the scanner's normal facility power sources and accessible disconnects or power controls are in their expected operating state. Check for signs of a recent outage, utility interruption, generator transfer, breaker event, or room power problem. Do not reset facility electrical equipment unless authorized by site procedure. Expected outcome: Required power sources are present and no obvious facility power interruption remains. If facility power was the cause and the CT system starts normally after authorized restoration, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Emergency-Stop and Safety Controls
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible emergency-stop controls and other external safety interlocks for an activated, damaged, or abnormal condition. Do not bypass or defeat any interlock. Expected outcome: No emergency-stop or external safety control is preventing normal startup. If an activated control is safely restored according to approved procedure and startup completes normally, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect External Connections and Workstation Power
steps.instructions: Check accessible power cords, workstation power connections, display connections, and external communication cables for looseness, damage, or accidental disconnection. Reseat only user-accessible or service-approved connections. Expected outcome: External connections are secure and undamaged. If restoring an external connection resolves startup, complete functional verification and stop.

steps.title: 6. Verify Operator Workstation and Display Operation
steps.instructions: Determine whether the workstation, monitors, keyboard, mouse, and other operator-interface components are powered and responsive. A blank display can be mistaken for a scanner startup failure. Expected outcome: The operator interface powers normally and accepts input. If the scanner was operating but the workstation or display connection was the only problem, correct the external cause and verify normal control.

steps.title: 7. Check Room and Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Look for excessive heat, blocked equipment-room ventilation, water intrusion, unusual odor, smoke, or evidence of a cooling problem. Do not continue powering equipment that shows evidence of overheating, electrical damage, water exposure, or burning odor. Expected outcome: Environmental conditions are suitable for continued evaluation. If an unsafe environmental condition is present, remove the equipment from service and escalate immediately.

steps.title: 8. Perform an Approved Controlled Restart if Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the system is stable, no patient is dependent on it, and site/manufacturer procedures permit it, perform a normal controlled shutdown and restart using approved operating controls. Do not repeatedly cycle system power in response to recurring failures. Expected outcome: The CT system completes its normal startup sequence without recurring faults. If startup completes and remains stable, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm that the operator workstation is responsive, required scanner subsystems indicate ready status, gantry and table controls are available, and no unresolved startup or safety messages remain. Use approved operational checks before returning the scanner to clinical use. Expected outcome: The CT system starts normally and reaches a stable ready condition. If achieved, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Startup Failure
steps.instructions: If the system still will not start or initialize, stop external troubleshooting. Do not proceed into power distribution assemblies, cabinets, internal electronics, or restricted service functions without appropriate authorization and documentation. Expected outcome: An unresolved system is kept out of clinical service and routed for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: CT staff reported the Aquilion ONE / PRISM Edition would not complete startup after a facility power interruption.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found facility power had been restored but an accessible system power connection had not returned to its normal operating condition.
CCR.Resolution: Restored the approved external power condition, confirmed successful system startup and ready status, and verified normal operator controls before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the entire system or only the workstation was affected.
Recent power outage or generator transfer.
Evidence of heat, odor, water, or damage.

title: Canon Aquilion ONE / PRISM Edition CT Scanner - Workstation Freezes or Loses Communication
description: Addresses workstation freezes or communication loss caused by power, cables, network connections, peripheral problems, software state, or infrastructure interruptions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Preserve Examination Data
steps.instructions: Do not continue scanning when the operator workstation is unreliable or communication with the scanner is lost. If a patient is on the table, safely conclude or terminate the examination according to approved clinical procedures and use alternate imaging if needed. Expected outcome: The patient is protected and unnecessary data loss is minimized.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the workstation is completely frozen, only one application is unresponsive, communication with the gantry is lost, or the display/input devices are not responding. Record displayed messages exactly. Expected outcome: The problem is clearly defined.

steps.title: 3. Check Workstation Power and Peripherals
steps.instructions: Verify workstation power, monitor status, keyboard, mouse, and other accessible peripherals. Inspect external power and data connections for looseness or damage. Expected outcome: A peripheral or simple power issue is either corrected or ruled out.

steps.title: 4. Check Scanner-to-Workstation Connectivity
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible network and system communication cables between approved external connection points. Do not disconnect internal scanner communication wiring. Expected outcome: External communication connections are secure. If reseating an approved external connection restores stable communication, continue to functional verification.

steps.title: 5. Determine Whether the Problem Is Local or Network-Wide
steps.instructions: Ask whether other networked systems are experiencing communication problems and whether the CT scanner remains responsive locally. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to the CT workstation or a broader infrastructure issue.

steps.title: 6. Check for Recent Power or Network Events
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem followed an outage, network change, switch maintenance, software update, or system restart. Expected outcome: Relevant recent events are identified.

steps.title: 7. Perform an Approved Controlled Workstation Restart
steps.instructions: If no active patient procedure depends on the workstation and approved procedures permit it, perform a normal controlled restart. Avoid repeated hard power-offs unless required by authorized service procedures. Expected outcome: The workstation restarts and re-establishes stable communication.

steps.title: 8. Verify Scanner and Application Communication
steps.instructions: Confirm that the workstation communicates with the scanner, expected system statuses populate normally, and required control functions are available. Expected outcome: Communication remains stable without recurring freezes.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Use an approved non-patient workflow to verify workstation responsiveness, scanner communication, study handling, and data availability. Expected outcome: The workstation remains responsive and required CT communication functions normally. If achieved, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Recurrent Freeze or Communication Loss
steps.instructions: If freezing or communication loss returns, remove the scanner from service as appropriate. Do not modify restricted software, internal network configuration, operating-system files, or service applications without authorization. Expected outcome: An unreliable workstation is escalated before clinical use resumes.

CCR.Complaint: CT staff reported the operator workstation froze and lost communication with the scanner.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an accessible workstation network connection was loose.
CCR.Resolution: Secured the connection, restarted the workstation using the approved process, and verified stable scanner communication and normal non-patient workflow.

helpfulDetails: Whether the entire workstation or one application froze.
